title: THE ODDS RECEIPT
goal: Fear speaks in certainty; reality keeps percentages.
steps:
1. Score Odds — Give the prediction a number from 0 to 100.
2. Check Baseline — Find one real reference point: how often has this happened in similar situations?
3. Weigh Evidence — Notice one fact that raises the odds and another that lowers them.
4. Revise Odds — Pick a new number and remember it.
5. Follow Evidence — Act from the revision, not the original alarm.
win: ✓ Disaster stopped being the only ending.
supports:
• Exhale after “Follow Evidence”; leave the forecast.
• Loop back? Use “Weigh Evidence”.
• “Revise Odds” — fear isn’t fate.
• What lost power: “Score Odds” → “Follow Evidence”?
• I can use “Check Baseline” while fear stays loud.
formula_flow: Score Odds → Check Baseline → Weigh Evidence → Revise Odds → Follow Evidence
safety:
PAUSE
End the count if numbers become reassurance checking or you cannot stop recalculating.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: THE BAD VOICE ACTOR
goal: Authority often hides inside delivery.
steps:
1. Read Wrong — Hear the thought as a tired GPS, an overdramatic sports commentator, or a hesitant intern reading the wrong memo.
2. Keep Words — Keep the words unchanged; alter only tempo, pitch, and confidence.
3. Replay — Then replay it in your natural voice as a possibility, not an order.
win: ✓ A fixed rule turned back into a context-dependent idea.
supports:
• Exhale after “Replay”; loosen the label.
• Shortcut: “Keep Words”, once.
• “Keep Words” — the rule loosened.
• “Read Wrong” versus “Replay”: what eased?
• I can use “Keep Words” without becoming the label.
formula_flow: Read Wrong → Keep Words → Replay
safety:
PAUSE
Use a neutral voice instead if playful recasting feels shaming or agitating.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: EDIT THE FONT, NOT YOURSELF
goal: A thought displayed differently can be held differently.
steps:
1. Project — Project the sentence on an inner screen.
2. Shrink — Shrink it to caption size.
3. Move Metres — Move it two metres away.
4. Lower Opacity — Lower opacity, swap the heavy typeface for something ordinary, and place generous blank space around it.
5. Read Version — Read the edited version once, then look at real text nearby.
win: ✓ The thought changed format, and some of its spell broke.
supports:
• Exhale after “Read Version”; loosen the label.
• Skip replay; use “Move Metres”.
• “Lower Opacity” — the rule loosened.
• At “Read Version”, compare “Project”.
• I can use “Shrink” without becoming the label.
formula_flow: Project → Shrink → Move Metres → Lower Opacity → Read Version

title: TENSION’S EXIT PARTNER
goal: Teach one muscle where release lives.
steps:
1. Select Safe — Select a safe body region.
2. Tighten — Tighten it lightly—not maximally—during an easy inhale.
3. Leave Muscle — As air leaves, let the muscle become heavy and wide.

title: DROP THE APPEAL
goal: Reality has already entered the room; the appeal is only in your mind.
steps:
1. State Fact — State the fact in plain past or present tense.
2. Remove Approval — Remove approval, blame, and every ‘should not have happened.’ Notice the body’s protest and answer, ‘Not liking it is allowed.
3. Add Nothing — Refusing its existence adds nothing.’ Choose the next response available in the world that actually exists.
win: ✓ I stopped appealing reality and moved inside the version that exists.

title: TURN AGAIN
goal: Acceptance is often a direction repeated, not a mood achieved.
steps:
1. Catch Mind — Catch the mind reopening the case against what has already occurred.
2. Name Refusal — Name the refusal without criticism.
3. Rotate Attention — Rotate attention toward the existing fact and the action now possible.
4. Return Wheel — Each return is one turn of the wheel; stop counting after the chosen behaviour begins.
win: ✓ I turned back toward reality once more—and stopped counting when action began.
supports:
• Exhale after “Return Wheel”; drop the scoreboard.
• Catch restart with “Rotate Attention”.
• “Rotate Attention” keeps worth off scoreboards.
• What changed: “Catch Mind” → “Return Wheel”?
• I can use “Name Refusal” without ranking my worth.
formula_flow: Catch Mind → Name Refusal → Rotate Attention → Return Wheel

title: PUT GOOD ON THE CALENDAR
goal: Positive events need appointments, not vague hope.
steps:
1. Choose Genuinely — Choose one really reinforcing experience; assign it a time, place, and first action.
2. Protect Appointment — Protect the appointment from unnecessary multitasking.
3. Details — While it happens, notice three details worth encoding.
4. Lock It In — Afterward, resist grading whether you enjoyed it ‘enough.’
win: ✓ Good got a place on the calendar without needing a score.
supports:
• Exhale after “Lock It In”; let feeling settle.
• On return: “Details”.
• “Details” separates feeling from fact.
• “Choose Genuinely” versus “Lock It In”: what eased?
• I can use “Protect Appointment” while emotion stays loud.
formula_flow: Choose Genuinely → Protect Appointment → Details → Lock It In

title: BORROW THE SENSATION
goal: Teach the body that a safe signal is not the worst-case story.
steps:
1. Select Medically — Select a medically safe exercise that creates a mild feared sensation—brief spinning, stair walking, or breathing through a narrow straw only when appropriate.
2. Test Sensation — Predict what will happen, induce the sensation briefly, and observe recovery without usual calming it.
win: ✓ I predicted the sensation, borrowed it briefly, and watched my body recover.
supports:
• Gently exhale after “Test Sensation”; no forcing.
• On return: “Test Sensation”.
• “Select Medically” keeps sensation as data.
• “Select Medically” → “Test Sensation”: what changed?
• I can use “Test Sensation” while sensation stays.

title: PENDULUM BETWEEN TWO TRUTHS
goal: Regulation can be built by travelling, not staying still.
steps:
1. Find Activated — Find one activated region and another settled or supported area.
2. Move Resource — Touch the difficult region with attention for a few seconds, then move to the resource.
3. Travel — Travel back and forth at a pace that preserves choice.
4. Finish Whichever — Finish on whichever location offers steadier awareness of your location.
win: ✓ Certainty remained unavailable; movement did not.

• If it flares, choose “Travel”.
• “Travel” keeps uncertainty carryable.
• “Find Activated” versus “Finish Whichever”: what eased?
• I can use “Move Resource” without a guarantee.

title: WAIT FOR THE WHOLE BODY ANSWER
goal: Some experience forms before it can be explained.
steps:
1. Bring Mind — Bring the issue to mind lightly, then pause verbal analysis.
2. Ask Body — Ask the body, ‘What is the whole of this like?’ Wait for an image, phrase, posture, or global texture.
3. Check Whether — Check whether it fits by noticing a small inner yes, no, or shift.
4. Leave It Raw — Leave the answer unpolished.
win: ✓ The body answered before language polished it.
supports:

• If it flares, choose “Check Whether”.
• “Check Whether” keeps uncertainty carryable.
• “Leave It Raw”: what changed from “Bring Mind”?
• I can use “Ask Body” without a guarantee.

content:
TITLE
WAIT FOR THE WHOLE BODY ANSWER

GOAL
Some experience forms before it can be explained.

RITUAL
1. Bring Mind — Bring the issue to mind lightly, then pause verbal analysis.
2. Ask Body — Ask the body, ‘What is the whole of this like?’ Wait for an image, phrase, posture, or global texture.
3. Check Whether — Check whether it fits by noticing a small inner yes, no, or shift.
4. Leave It Raw — Leave the answer unpolished.

WIN
✓ The body answered before language polished it.

• Exhale after “Leave It Raw”; leave it unanswered.
• If it flares, choose “Check Whether”.
• “Check Whether” keeps uncertainty carryable.
• “Leave It Raw”: what changed from “Bring Mind”?
• I can use “Ask Body” without a guarantee.

FORMULA FLOW
Bring Mind → Ask Body → Check Whether → Leave It Raw

PAUSE
End the inquiry if bodily attention creates panic, numbness, or feeling unreal or disconnected.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: COMPLETE THE DEFENCE IN MINIATURE
goal: An interrupted protective move may still be waiting.
steps:
1. Small — Notice the small impulse to push, turn, step back, shield, or say no.
2. Let Unfold — In a safe space, let it unfold slowly at ten percent strength.
3. Stop Completion — Stop at the natural completion and return to neutral posture.
4. Observe Whether — Observe whether the body receives an ending.
win: ✓ The urge peaked without becoming a contract.
supports:
• Exhale after “Observe Whether”; let wanting crest.
• Use “Stop Completion” on return.
• “Stop Completion” keeps wanting off controls.
• “Observe Whether”: what changed from “Small”?
• I can use “Let Unfold” without obeying the urge.
formula_flow: Small → Let Unfold → Stop Completion → Observe Whether

title: FIND THE BODY’S WORKABLE DISTANCE
goal: Boundaries can be measured before they are argued.
steps:
1. Use Object — Using an object, doorway, or trusted person with consent, test near and far in small increments.
2. Breath — Notice breath, posture, urge, and clarity at each point.
3. Body — Notice where the body can stay present and communicate.
4. Set Workable Distance — That distance is data, not a permanent verdict.
win: ✓ The body found a workable distance without turning it into a verdict.
supports:

• Re-entry move: “Body”.
• “Body” keeps wanting off controls.
• “Set Workable Distance”: what changed from “Use Object”?
• I can use “Breath” without obeying the urge.

title: BORROW THE FLOOR
goal: Let external support do part of the holding.
steps:
1. Choose Contact — Choose one contact point—feet, seat, back, forearms, or hands.
2. Release Extra — Increase pressure slightly, then release extra effort and notice what the surface continues to carry.
3. Name Texture — Name its texture, temperature, and steadiness.
4. Trust Ground — You need not manufacture a sense of ground.
win: ✓ The present regained enough detail to hold me.
supports:
• Exhale after “Trust Ground”; notice the room.
• On return: “Name Texture”.
• “Name Texture” proves the present returned.
• At “Trust Ground”, compare “Choose Contact”.
• I can use “Release Extra” to return here.
formula_flow: Choose Contact → Release Extra → Name Texture → Trust Ground

title: CATCH THE RECOVERY SIGNAL
goal: Settling deserves as much attention as alarm.
steps:
1. Watch Swallow — After body alarm, watch for a swallow, sigh, warmth, trembling, yawn, moisture in the eyes, breath shift, or muscle release.
2. Name Accurately — When one appears, name it accurately and stay with its after-effect.
3. No Extra Trigger — Do not provoke more.
4. Look Like — Teach the mind what recovery looks like.
win: ✓ The alarm stayed loud, but the world got wider.
supports:
• Exhale after “Look Like”; leave it unanswered.
• Restart detected: “No Extra Trigger”.
• “No Extra Trigger” keeps uncertainty carryable.
• “Watch Swallow” versus “Look Like”: what eased?
• I can use “Name Accurately” without a guarantee.

Settling deserves as much attention as alarm.

• “No Extra Trigger” keeps uncertainty carryable.

• I can use “Name Accurately” without a guarantee.

Watch Swallow → Name Accurately → No Extra Trigger → Look Like

Seek care if shaking, breathing changes, or other symptoms seem medically concerning.

goal: Do not close the file while the body is still asking for attention.
steps:

title: FIND THE BUSY HALF
goal: Not every unsettled breath needs a longer exhale.
steps:
1. Observe Ordinary — Observe three ordinary cycles.
2. Rate Inhale — Rate inhale effort and exhale release separately.
3. Phase — Which phase is working too hard?
4. Leave Timing — Ease only that side toward neutral—less pulling in or less pushing out—while leaving timing alone.
5. Check Whether — Check if urgency changes when imbalance decreases.
win: ✓ Comparison lost its right to set my value.
supports:
• Exhale after “Check Whether”; drop the scoreboard.
• Re-entry move: “Phase”.
• “Leave Timing” keeps worth off scoreboards.
• Compare “Observe Ordinary” with “Check Whether”.
• I can use “Rate Inhale” without ranking my worth.
formula_flow: Observe Ordinary → Rate Inhale → Phase → Leave Timing → Check Whether

1. Observe Ordinary — Observe three ordinary cycles.

4. Leave Timing — Ease only that side toward neutral—less pulling in or less pushing out—while leaving timing alone.
5. Check Whether — Check if urgency changes when imbalance decreases.

• “Leave Timing” keeps worth off scoreboards.

title: ALTERNATE THE AIRWAY
goal: Move attention left and right until state feels organised.
steps:
1. Sit Easy — Sit comfortably.
2. Close Nostril — Without force, close one nostril and breathe through the other; switch sides for the next gentle cycle.
3. Continue Unhurried — Continue alternating with an unhurried hand.
4. Keep Breath — Keep the breath quiet and abandon retention.
5. Open Both Sides — Finish with both sides open and let breathing return to normal.
win: ✓ Left, right, centre: attention finished organised and unforced.
supports:
• Gently exhale after “Open Both Sides”; no forcing.
• Use “Continue Unhurried” on return.
• “Keep Breath” keeps sensation as data.
• “Sit Easy” → “Open Both Sides”: what changed?
• I can use “Close Nostril” while sensation stays.
formula_flow: Sit Easy → Close Nostril → Continue Unhurried → Keep Breath → Open Both Sides

title: VIBRATION ON THE WAY OUT
goal: Let sound carry the exhale without squeezing it.
steps:
1. Take Ordinary — Take an ordinary inhale.
2. Leave Feeling — Hum at a soft, comfortable pitch as air leaves, feeling vibration in lips, face, or chest.
3. Stop Empty — Stop before empty.
4. Listen Silence — Listen to the silence after the hum, then decide whether another round would still feel kind.
win: ✓ The current moment has edges again.
supports:
• Exhale after “Listen Silence”; then keep moving.
• Loop back? Use “Stop Empty”.
• “Stop Empty” proves motion is available.
• At “Listen Silence”, compare “Take Ordinary”.
• I can use “Leave Feeling” before motivation.
formula_flow: Take Ordinary → Leave Feeling → Stop Empty → Listen Silence

content:
TITLE
VIBRATION ON THE WAY OUT

GOAL
Let sound carry the exhale without squeezing it.

RITUAL
1. Take Ordinary — Take an ordinary inhale.
2. Leave Feeling — Hum at a soft, comfortable pitch as air leaves, feeling vibration in lips, face, or chest.
3. Stop Empty — Stop before empty.
4. Listen Silence — Listen to the silence after the hum, then decide whether another round would still feel kind.

WIN
✓ The current moment has edges again.

• Exhale after “Listen Silence”; then keep moving.
• Loop back? Use “Stop Empty”.
• “Stop Empty” proves motion is available.
• At “Listen Silence”, compare “Take Ordinary”.
• I can use “Leave Feeling” before motivation.

FORMULA FLOW
Take Ordinary → Leave Feeling → Stop Empty → Listen Silence

PAUSE
Cease with pain, coughing, light-headedness, or vocal discomfort.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: COOL AIR, WARM DECISION
goal: Borrow a settling cue from temperature.
steps:
1. Imagine Mild — Shape the lips or tongue only if comfortable, notice a mild stream of cool air, and let exhalation leave naturally through the nose.
2. Coolness — Notice coolness rather than volume.
3. End After — Stop after a few easy cycles and choose one unhurried action.
win: ✓ Cooling changed the body volume before the mind wrote the explanation.
supports:
• Exhale after “End After”; notice the room.
• Shortcut: “Coolness”, once.
• “Coolness” proves the present returned.
• “Imagine Mild” → “End After”: what changed?
• I can use “Coolness” to return here.
formula_flow: Imagine Mild → Coolness → End After

title: THE RETURN REP
goal: Attention strengthens on the comeback, not the stay.
steps:
1. Select Neutral — Select one neutral anchor.
2. Attention — Each time distraction appears, notice where attention went and escort it back without commentary.
3. Count Rather — Count returns rather than uninterrupted seconds.
4. End After — Finish after ten honest comebacks, even if focus never felt perfect.
win: ✓ Ten returns happened. Perfect focus was never required.
supports:
• Exhale after “End After”; release the score.
• Skip replay; use “Count Rather”.
• “Count Rather” keeps progress moving imperfectly.
• Look back: “Select Neutral” → “End After”.
• I can use “Attention” without perfecting.
formula_flow: Select Neutral → Attention → Count Rather → End After

title: BEFORE THE SENTENCE
goal: Look for thought at the moment of assembly.
steps:

2. Earliest — When a thought begins, notice its earliest form: pressure, fragment, image, word, or felt orientation in space.
3. No Backtracking — Do not chase backward after it fully forms.
4. Catch the Birth — Simply Notice ‘birth’ and let the completed thought continue.

title: THE RETURN CHAIN
goal: Ongoing sense is built from linked renewals.
steps:

2. Set Cue — Define its cue, duration, and one tiny restart signal.
3. Return Repetition — Each session begins with the final second of yesterday’s intention: ‘return again.’ Protect repetition from heroic increases.
4. Link the Return — A chain is made of modest links.

title: TRACE THE FIRST SPARK
goal: Find what started the fluctuation before content took over.
steps:
1. Take Recurring — Take one recurring state and move backward through its chain: current thought, preceding sensation, image, memory, external cue, and hidden tendency.
2. Stop Earliest — Stop at the earliest condition you can really spot.
3. Mark the Spark — Notice the point where future interruption could happen.
win: ✓ The spark became visible early enough to interrupt next time.
supports:
• Exhale after “Mark the Spark”; let feeling settle.
• On return: “Stop Earliest”.
• “Stop Earliest” separates feeling from fact.
• “Take Recurring” to “Mark the Spark”: what loosened?
• I can use “Stop Earliest” while emotion stays loud.

title: FIND WHERE THE PATTERN MISSED
goal: One exception is enough to weaken inevitability.
steps:
1. Name Pattern — Name the recurring pattern in one line, including the trigger and usual response.
2. Find Misses — Find two occasions when the same kind of trigger produced no pattern or a clearly weaker version.
3. Compare Conditions — Compare the exceptions. Spot one shared condition that you can influence: timing, preparation, company, distance, information, or body care.
4. Transplant Edge — Place that condition into the next comparable situation and define what weaker would look like.
win: ✓ The pattern already has an exception; inevitability just lost ground.
supports:
• Gently exhale after “Transplant Edge”; no forcing.
• Loop back? Use “Compare Conditions”.
• “Compare Conditions” keeps sensation as data.
• At “Transplant Edge”, compare “Name Pattern”.
• I can use “Find Misses” while sensation stays.
formula_flow: Name Pattern → Find Misses → Compare Conditions → Transplant Edge

title: RUN THE START GATE TWICE
goal: The first start can be rehearsal; the second one becomes real.
steps:
1. Stage Door — Choose the opening movements: open the file, place the tool, find the line, or position your hands. Keep it under ten seconds.
2. Dry Launch — do that sequence once without producing work. Stop at the edge of action; this is the dry launch.
3. Full Reset — Return your hands or screen to neutral exactly once. Leave the plan unchanged or add another rehearsal.
4. Live Entry — Repeat the same sequence and continue straight into thirty seconds of real work.
win: ✓ The pain kept its truth while life kept another department open.
supports:
• Exhale after “Live Entry”; keep the compass.
• If it flares, choose “Full Reset”.
• “Full Reset” keeps meaning in motion.
• “Stage Door” to “Live Entry”: what loosened?
• I can use “Dry Launch” while pain stays real.
formula_flow: Stage Door → Dry Launch → Full Reset → Live Entry

title: ROTATE THE CHAIR
goal: One perspective is data, not the whole room.
steps:
1. Describe Event — Describe the event from your position.
2. Move Seats — Move seats and say what the other person might perceive, labelling guesses.
3. Watch Behaviour — Stand as a neutral observer and keep only observable behaviour.
4. Ask Future — Finally, ask what future-you would wish had happened next.
win: ✓ The conversation gained structure instead of more force.
supports:
• Exhale after “Ask Future”; soften the jaw.
• On return: “Watch Behaviour”.
• “Watch Behaviour” keeps clarity above heat.
• “Ask Future”: what changed from “Describe Event”?
• I can use “Move Seats” without extra heat.

title: MOVE THE HEAVIEST WORD
goal: Move the emphasis and find where the sentence keeps its weight.
steps:
1. Say Alarm — Choose the exact alarm sentence and shorten it to seven words or fewer.
2. Shift Stress — Say it quietly several times, moving emphasis to one different word per round. Keep pitch and speed comfortable.
3. Find Weight — Notice which emphasis changes the meaning or body response most. Focus only on that word.
4. Keep Signal — Keep the weighted word as information; stop the repetitions without debating the whole sentence.
win: ✓ I found the word carrying the weight and stopped rehearsing the whole sentence.
supports:
• Gently exhale after “Keep Signal”; no breath-holding.
• Re-entry move: “Find Weight”.
• “Find Weight” — alarm isn’t command.
• Before/after: “Say Alarm” → “Keep Signal”.
• I can use “Shift Stress” while alarm rises.
formula_flow: Say Alarm → Shift Stress → Find Weight → Keep Signal

title: A PLACE FOR THE LOSS
goal: Grief needs a deliberate address in time.
steps:
1. Choose Object — Choose an object, date, location, and act of remembrance.
2. Say Name — Say the name of what was lost, honour what remains meaningful, and name a farewell to what cannot continue.
3. Close Bond — Close by deciding how the bond or value will be carried forward.
win: ✓ A meaningful next step survived the heaviness.
supports:

• Restart detected: “Say Name”.
• “Say Name” keeps meaning in motion.
• Look back: “Choose Object” → “Close Bond”.
• I can use “Say Name” while pain stays real.

title: CHANGE THE OBJECT, MARK THE RELEASE
goal: Let matter carry a decision the mind keeps reopening.
steps:
1. Picture Safe — Picture or select a safe symbol for what you are relinquishing.
2. Choose Transformation — Choose a transformation that fits: fold, seal, store, shred, bury where lawful, or dissolve safely.
3. Name Responsibility — Name what is ending and what responsibility remains.
4. Mark the Release — Complete the physical change once.
win: ✓ The object changed once; the decision got a physical full stop.
supports:
• Exhale after “Mark the Release”; soften the jaw.
• Return once to “Name Responsibility”.
• “Name Responsibility” keeps clarity above heat.
• “Mark the Release”: what changed from “Picture Safe”?
• I can use “Choose Transformation” without extra heat.
formula_flow: Picture Safe → Choose Transformation → Name Responsibility → Mark the Release

content:
TITLE
CHANGE THE OBJECT, MARK THE RELEASE

GOAL
Let matter carry a decision the mind keeps reopening.

RITUAL
1. Picture Safe — Picture or select a safe symbol for what you are relinquishing.
2. Choose Transformation — Choose a transformation that fits: fold, seal, store, shred, bury where lawful, or dissolve safely.
3. Name Responsibility — Name what is ending and what responsibility remains.
4. Mark the Release — Complete the physical change once.

WIN
✓ The object changed once; the decision got a physical full stop.

• Exhale after “Mark the Release”; soften the jaw.
• Return once to “Name Responsibility”.
• “Name Responsibility” keeps clarity above heat.
• “Mark the Release”: what changed from “Picture Safe”?
• I can use “Choose Transformation” without extra heat.

FORMULA FLOW
Picture Safe → Choose Transformation → Name Responsibility → Mark the Release

PAUSE
Never burn, bury, ingest, or destroy items unsafely or illegally.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: TODAY’S FURTHEST USEFUL HORIZON
goal: Not every distant scenario deserves a seat in this decision.
steps:
1. Ask Far — Ask how far ahead consequences can meaningfully alter today’s move: tonight, one week, six months.
2. Imagine Line — Imagine a line at that horizon.
3. Park Scenario — Park every scenario beyond it unless it changes a present safety or commitment fact.
4. Decide Information — Decide using information inside the line.
win: ✓ The decision stayed inside today’s useful horizon.
supports:
• Exhale after “Decide Information”; end the lap.
• On return: “Park Scenario”.
• “Park Scenario” proves loops can stop.
• Compare “Ask Far” with “Decide Information”.
• I can use “Imagine Line” without another lap.
formula_flow: Ask Far → Imagine Line → Park Scenario → Decide Information

title: TURN THE LABEL INTO MOTION
goal: Turn the label into a process you can interrupt.
steps:
1. Take Identity — Take the identity or label word dominating the moment.
2. Translate Active — Translate it into active, time-specific verbs ending in -ing: withdrawing, scanning, grieving, protecting, predicting.
3. Ask Strengthens — Ask what starts, strengthens, interrupts, and ends that process.
win: ✓ The noun lost its cage; motion exposed a change point.
supports:
• Exhale after “Ask Strengthens”; soften the jaw.
• On return, repeat “Translate Active”.
• “Translate Active” keeps clarity above heat.
• What changed: “Take Identity” → “Ask Strengthens”?
• I can use “Translate Active” without extra heat.
formula_flow: Take Identity → Translate Active → Ask Strengthens
safety:
PAUSE
Do not discard formal diagnoses needed for treatment or access to support.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: MEANING ON HOLD
goal: Meaning must wait for independent witnesses.
steps:
1. Hold Event — Hold the event without explaining it.
2. Find Facts — Find three facts from different channels—what was said, what was observed, what occurred over time.
3. Name Meaning — Until all three exist, name every meaning temporary.
4. Assign Narrowest — Then assign the narrowest meaning supported.
win: ✓ I put meaning on hold until the facts had enough witnesses.
supports:
• Exhale after “Assign Narrowest”; soften the jaw.
• Re-entry move: “Name Meaning”.
• “Name Meaning” keeps clarity above heat.
• Keep one lesson: “Hold Event” → “Assign Narrowest”.
• I can use “Find Facts” without extra heat.
formula_flow: Hold Event → Find Facts → Name Meaning → Assign Narrowest

title: ONE WORD, ONE BREATH, RELEASE
goal: Compress the noise without pretending it is solved.
steps:
1. Choose Temporary — Choose a temporary word that holds the issue: betrayal, pressure, uncertainty, loss.
2. Say During — Say it once during a natural breath, feel its weight, and let the word leave with the breath’s end.
3. Keep One Name — Do not replace it with a second Name for thirty seconds.
win: ✓ One word rode one breath, then left without needing a replacement.
supports:
• Exhale after “Keep One Name”; leave it unanswered.
• Skip replay; use “Say During”.
• “Say During” keeps uncertainty carryable.
• Look back: “Choose Temporary” → “Keep One Name”.
• I can use “Say During” without a guarantee.
formula_flow: Choose Temporary → Say During → Keep One Name

title: TURN DOWN THE DOMINANT CHANNEL
goal: A memory can feel present because one sense owns the mix.
steps:
1. Identify Loudest — Spot the loudest recall channel—image, sound, touch, smell.
2. Reduce Brightness — Reduce its brightness, volume, proximity, or texture slightly.
3. Anchor the Present — At the same time, strengthen neutral present-day context: the room layout, today’s date, your clothing, or a distant sound.
win: ✓ Memory lost the whole screen; the present regained channels.
supports:
• Exhale after “Anchor the Present”; keep both sides.
• Skip replay; use “Reduce Brightness”.
• “Reduce Brightness” widens the evidence field.
• “Anchor the Present”: what changed from “Identify Loudest”?
• I can use “Reduce Brightness” before concluding.

title: SET THE LIMIT BEFORE THE NEXT TEST
goal: Decide the enforcement rule while the room is calm.
steps:
1. Count Pattern — Define the behaviour in terms a camera could Keep.
2. Set Threshold — Choose the count, duration, or date that will Notice the limit.
3. Link Consequence — Attach one consequence under your control, such as ending the call, leaving, or changing access.
4. Follow Contract — If the threshold is crossed, follow the contract once without holding a motive trial.
win: ✓ The boundary was decided in calm, so motive did not get a retrial.
supports:
• Exhale after “Follow Contract”; release extra load.
• On return: “Link Consequence”.
• “Link Consequence” keeps responsibility proportionate.
• Difference check: “Count Pattern” → “Follow Contract”.
• I can use “Set Threshold” without carrying it all.

goal: Reduce aggression preparation without weakening the sentence.
steps:

4. Let Articulation — Let articulation stay clear while muscular threat signalling drops.

• On return, repeat “Deliver Limit”.

• At “Let Articulation”, compare “Notice Jaw”.
• I can use “Separate Teeth” without carrying it all.

title: CHANGE THE MENTAL TOOL, NOT THE PRESSURE
goal: Wrong mental mode makes effort repeat itself.
steps:
1. Decide Accept — Classify the demand as SOLVE, DECIDE, FEEL, ACCEPT, COMMUNICATE, or WAIT.
2. Name Mode — Name the mode currently running.
3. Choose Shut — Shut it down and do the first action belonging to the correct mode—calculate, choose, allow, release, speak, or schedule.
win: ✓ I changed mental tools instead of pushing the wrong one harder.
supports:
• Gently exhale after “Choose Shut”; orient to now.
• Use “Name Mode” on return.
• “Name Mode” moves memory toward then.
• What changed: “Decide Accept” → “Choose Shut”?
• I can use “Name Mode” while staying in now.
formula_flow: Decide Accept → Name Mode → Choose Shut
safety:
PAUSE
